review_evidence: Focused schema, runtime hash, pedagogy quality, and key self-review for eng_c3_ch06 on 2026-07-12
title: Paper Boats
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Find the story setting
levels.teaching_goal: Use place and object clues to understand where a story begins and what the main play activity is.

guided_check.teaching_block: In a paper boat story, setting clues matter. A stream, flowing water, and a small folded boat tell us where the action begins.
guided_check.passage: Meera stands near clear flowing water. She places a folded paper boat on the water and watches it move.
guided_check.prompt: Where does Meera put the paper boat?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: ask where the object can move. A paper boat moves in water, not on a shelf.
bridge.passage: A folded paper boat floats away slowly.
bridge.prompt: What helps a paper boat float away?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: setting is the story place. Object clues like boat, float, and stream all point to water.
masterclass.passage: A child drops a small folded boat and watches it sail past a bamboo bridge.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now identify the main object without hints.
independent_check.passage: The children fold coloured sheets and place them in the flowing water.
independent_check.prompt: What are the children playing with?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use setting and action clues in a different kind of floating experiment. Separate the place from the object being tested.
transfer_check.passage: At science club, children place dry leaves in a wide tub. The leaves drift from one end of the water to the other.

levels.title: Explain a character feeling
levels.teaching_goal: Connect a character's feeling to the action that caused it.

guided_check.teaching_block: A feeling answer should not only name the feeling. It should also explain what caused it.
guided_check.passage: A boy keeps turning Rina's paper boats upside down. Rina tells him to stop.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: look for the problem. If someone spoils your work, anger is a likely feeling.
bridge.passage: Rina worked carefully. Then the boy spoiled the boats again and again.
bridge.prompt: Which feeling best matches Rina's reaction?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: make the answer complete with because. Feeling plus reason makes the response stronger.
masterclass.passage: The boy overturned Rina's boats after she had made them carefully.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer gives the reason clearly?
options: She was angry because he overturned her boats
She was angry because the sky was blue
She was happy because he spoiled them
She was sleepy because of the stream
accepted_answers: she was angry because he overturned her boats

independent_check.teaching_block: Read a new event, identify the feeling, and support it with the event that caused it.
independent_check.passage: Tara's boat reaches the bend, but a sudden splash tears its paper sail. Tara sighs and picks up the pieces.
independent_check.prompt: How does Tara probably feel, and why?

concept_slots.description: Names a fitting unhappy feeling.
Explains that the splash tore or damaged the boat.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer feeling-plus-cause reasoning to a team activity. Do not guess from one emotion word; use what happened.
transfer_check.passage: Imran builds a block tower for the class display. A teammate bumps the table, then quickly helps him rebuild it. Imran smiles at the teammate.
transfer_check.prompt: How does Imran feel at the end, and what caused that feeling?

concept_slots.description: Names a fitting positive feeling at the end.
Explains that the teammate helped rebuild the tower.

levels.title: Follow the helping sequence
levels.teaching_goal: Understand how a conflict changes into cooperation when one character teaches another.

guided_check.teaching_block: The story changes when the child who caused trouble admits he wants to play too. Then the helper shows the steps instead of only scolding.
guided_check.passage: The boy says he does not know how to make a paper boat. Rina shows him how to fold the paper.
guided_check.prompt: What action does Rina teach the boy?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: if someone does not know a making step, the helper can show the step.
bridge.passage: Rina takes a sheet and bends it neatly to make a boat shape.
bridge.prompt: Which word names the making action?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: sequence the help. First she gives paper, then she shows folding, then both children float boats.
masterclass.passage: First Rina shares paper. Next she teaches the folds. After that, both boats float.
masterclass.prompt: What does Rina do before both children float boats?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now answer the helping action without hints.
independent_check.passage: The boy could not make a boat. Rina used a sheet to teach him the folds.
independent_check.prompt: How did Rina help the boy?
accepted_answers: showed him how to make a boat
she showed him how to make a boat
showed him how to fold paper

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the helping-sequence idea to a skill outside paper folding. Name the useful action, not just the object.
transfer_check.passage: Leela cannot tie the cord around a parcel. Omar loosens the knot, shows the loop slowly, and lets Leela try again.
accepted_answers: shows her how to tie the knot
teaches her to tie the cord
he shows her how to make the loop

levels.title: Use he and she
levels.teaching_goal: Replace a repeated naming word with he or she while keeping the sentence clear.

guided_check.teaching_block: Pronouns help us avoid repeating a name. Use she for a girl or woman, and he for a boy or man.
guided_check.passage: Rina likes making paper boats. ___ folds the paper carefully.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: look at the person named first. Rina is a girl, so the next sentence can use she.
bridge.passage: Rina shares her paper. ___ helps her friend.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: choose the pronoun from the noun. Boy takes he. Girl takes she.
masterclass.passage: Aman watches the boat. ___ wants to make one too.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use a pronoun to avoid repeating a name, then complete the thought with the given action.
independent_check.passage: Sahil has a striped paper boat. Action: places it beside the blue boat.
independent_check.prompt: Write a second sentence about Sahil using he.

concept_slots.description: Uses he for Sahil.
Says that he places the boat beside the blue boat.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same pronoun strategy in a garden report. Make the reference clear before adding a new action.
transfer_check.passage: Maya waters the bean plant. Action: measures its new leaf.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the next sentence using she.

concept_slots.description: Uses she for Maya.
States that she measures the new leaf.

levels.title: Use position words
levels.teaching_goal: Use position words such as in, on, and under to describe where things are.

guided_check.teaching_block: A position word tells where something is. Under means below something; on means touching the top.
guided_check.passage: The ball rolled below the chair.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: picture the object. If it is below the table, it is under the table.
bridge.passage: The paper boat is below the bridge.
bridge.prompt: Which word fits: The boat is ___ the bridge?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: compare on and under. On touches the top surface. Under is below it.
masterclass.passage: The folded paper rests on the desk before the child makes a boat.
masterclass.prompt: Which position word tells where the paper is?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the position word without hints.
independent_check.passage: The paper sheet is resting on the table.
independent_check.prompt: Which word tells the paper's position?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use a position word in a map-reading context. Picture the two landmarks before naming their relationship.
transfer_check.passage: On the playground map, the drinking-water tap is behind the basketball post.
transfer_check.prompt: Which word tells the tap's position?

items.passage: Rain fills a shallow lane. Naman folds a square page, sets the little boat down, and runs beside it as the water carries it away.
items.prompt: What is the paragraph mainly about?
options: Naman sailing a paper boat in rainwater
accepted_answers: Naman sailing a paper boat in rainwater
a paper boat floating in rainwater

items.passage: Two boats meet at a narrow drain. Their makers lift one boat out so the other can pass, then swap turns at the next bend.
items.prompt: Which idea best sums up the scene?
options: the children cooperate and take turns
accepted_answers: the children cooperate and take turns

items.passage: Pia writes her boat's name before placing it in the puddle. The ink spreads when the paper becomes wet.
items.prompt: What happens to the ink?

items.passage: A twig blocks the channel. Dev removes it, and the trapped boat moves forward again.
items.prompt: What makes the boat move again?

items.passage: Mira's boat reaches the finish line first after she tests three different folds.
items.prompt: How might Mira feel, and why?

concept_slots.description: Names a fitting positive feeling.
Links the feeling to the boat finishing first or successful testing.

items.passage: Arif's careful model becomes soggy before the race begins because someone leaves it in the rain.
items.prompt: Explain Arif's likely feeling with a reason.

concept_slots.description: Names a fitting unhappy feeling.
Explains that the model became soggy or was left in rain.

items.passage: The class cannot make sharp folds. Jiya presses each line with a ruler and demonstrates one step at a time.
items.prompt: How does Jiya help?
accepted_answers: presses each line with a ruler

items.passage: Rohan's sail keeps falling. Keerthi adds a small piece of tape where the sail joins the boat.
items.prompt: Name Keerthi's helpful action.
accepted_answers: she adds a piece of tape

items.passage: Anaya checks the water tray. ___ removes a fallen leaf.
items.prompt: Choose the pronoun for Anaya.

items.passage: Kunal carries the tray. ___ sets it near the window.
items.prompt: Write the missing pronoun.

items.passage: Nora folds a yellow boat. Action: draws two round windows on it.
items.prompt: Continue Nora's description with a complete sentence that begins with She.

concept_slots.description: Uses she for Nora.
States that she draws two round windows.

items.passage: Vikram finds a dry sheet. Action: folds it into a narrow canoe shape.
items.prompt: Write the next sentence using he.

concept_slots.description: Uses he for Vikram.
States that he folds the sheet into a canoe shape.

items.passage: The blue boat is below the footbridge.
items.prompt: Which position word can replace below?

items.passage: A paper flag stands between the two boats.
items.prompt: Which word tells the flag's position?

items.passage: The red canoe is behind the green raft.
items.prompt: Where is the green raft compared with the canoe?

items.passage: A gust pushes Neel's boat away from the finish, but his partner blocks the side channel with a stone.
items.prompt: Why does the partner block the side channel?

concept_slots.description: Mentions the boat moving away or entering the side channel.
Explains that the action keeps or guides the boat toward the finish.

items.passage: After the race, the children collect every wet paper piece from the drain.
items.prompt: Give a reason for this action.

concept_slots.description: Mentions collecting paper or cleaning the drain.
Gives a cleanliness, litter, or blockage reason.

items.passage: First the children draw flags. Then they attach the flags to toothpicks. Last, they fix the toothpicks to the boats.
items.prompt: What happens immediately before the flags are fixed to the boats?
options: the flags are attached to toothpicks
accepted_answers: the flags are attached to toothpicks

items.passage: Asha places a coin inside her boat. It tips over, so she removes the coin and tries a dry seed instead.
items.prompt: What does Asha learn from the two tests?
options: a heavy load can tip the boat
accepted_answers: a heavy load can tip the boat

items.passage: Report facts: Pari | silver boat | floats under the arch | reaches the red marker.
items.prompt: Write a clear report sentence using she for Pari.

concept_slots.description: Uses she for Pari.
Mentions the silver boat.
Says it floats under the arch.
Says it reaches the red marker.
